_meta.indication: Artesunate for Injection is an antimalarial indicated for the initial treatment of severe malaria in adult and pediatric patients; should always be followed by a complete course of an appropriate oral antimalarial regimen.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: SEAQUAMAT (South East Asian Quinine Artesunate Malaria Trial)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated (no NCT number provided in the review)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, randomized (1:1), active comparator trial of IV artesunate vs IV quinine
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 2 years of age and older with severe P. falciparum malaria in Southeast Asia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: In-hospital all-cause mortality measured to time of hospital discharge
pivotal_trials.result: In-hospital mortality 13.2% with IV artesunate vs 20.5% with IV quinine, OR 0.59 (95% CI: 0.44, 0.79, p=0.0002)

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated (no NCT number provided in the review)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, active comparator trial of IV/IM artesunate vs IV/IM quinine in children (supportive evidence)
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients younger than 15 years with severe P. falciparum malaria in Africa
pivotal_trials.endpoint: In-hospital mortality (primary); severe neurological sequelae at 28 days (secondary)
pivotal_trials.result: In-hospital mortality 8.5% with artesunate vs 10.9% with quinine, OR 0.75 (95% CI: 0.63, 0.90, p=0.0022)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%) occurring more frequently with IV artesunate in Trial 1 were acute renal failure requiring dialysis (8.9% vs 7.3% quinine), hemoglobinuria (6.7% vs 4.5%), and jaundice (2.3% vs 1.9%). Serious risks include post-treatment (delayed) hemolytic anemia severe enough to require transfusion and hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis.
target_moa: Artesunate is a semi-synthetic artemisinin; its mode of action involves iron-catalyzed cleavage of the endoperoxide bridge generating free radicals and alkylation of malaria-specific proteins, inhibiting growth/replication of Plasmodium. It is rapidly hydrolyzed to the active metabolite dihydroartemisinin (DHA), active against erythrocytic asexual blood-stage parasites.
modality: Small molecule (semi-synthetic anti-malarial in the class of artemisinins)

basis.text: The IND received fast track, breakthrough and orphan designations during development.

citations.quote: While under development multiple submissions were received and meetings held with the Agency and the IND received fast track, breakthrough and orphan designations.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation for Artesunate for Injection (severe malaria); application exempt from PREA pediatric study requirement due to Orphan Drug Designation.

citations.quote: Due to the Orphan Drug Designation, this application is exempt from the requirement to conduct pediatric studies under the Pediatric Research Equity Act; this was communicated to the U.S. Army on March 28, 2019; ownership of Orphan Drug Designation for Artesunate for Injection was subsequently transferred to Amivas.

basis.text: The NDA was designated Priority review.

summary.text: NDA 213036 was submitted under section 505(b)(2) as a rolling, priority review; during development the IND received fast track, breakthrough (9/11/18) and orphan designations, with orphan drug designation ultimately held by Amivas. It was approved first cycle for the initial treatment of severe malaria; no advisory committee was convened and it was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: During the Pre-NDA discussions in 2019, both the US Army and Amivas participated in multiple meetings with the Agency, and a request for NDA rolling review was submitted and granted. On August 12, 2019, Amivas, LLC, began their rolling review submission of NDA 213036 for Artesunate for Injection for the initial treatment of severe (b) (4) malaria in adults and children; NDA submission was completed on September 26, 2019.

requirement.text: 3851-1: Conduct a single-arm descriptive international study collecting data in women exposed to IV artesunate during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant.

citations.quote: 3851-1 Conduct a single-arm descriptive international study collecting data in women exposed to IV artesunate during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The study will collect information for a minimum of 7 years.

requirement.text: 3851-2: Conduct a 5-year surveillance study to evaluate the potential development of resistance to artesunate and DHA from ongoing antimalarial resistance monitoring programs.

citations.quote: 3851-2 Conduct a 5-year surveillance study to evaluate the potential development of resistance to artesunate and DHA as obtained from ongoing resistance monitoring programs on antimalarials.

requirement.text: 3851-3: Conduct a female fertility study in rats testing adverse effects of IV artesunate administered prior to and through mating and implantation per ICH S5(A) and GLP.

citations.quote: 3851-3 Conduct a female fertility study in rats that tests the adverse effects of intravenous artesunate when administered prior to mating and continued through mating and implantation in accordance with ICH S5(A) and 21 CFR 58 Good Laboratory Practice for Nonclinical Laboratory Studies.

requirement.text: 3851-4: Conduct an In Vivo Micronucleus Assay evaluating IV artesunate at doses achieving target-tissue exposure per OECD Guideline #474 and GLP.

citations.quote: 3851-4 Conduct an In Vivo Micronucleus Assay that evaluates intravenous artesunate at doses demonstrated to achieve exposure at the target tissue site(s) and in accordance with the OECD Guideline for the Testing of Chemicals #474 and 21 CFR Part 58 Good Laboratory Practice for Nonclinical Laboratory Studies.

requirement.text: 3851-5: Conduct a descriptive 5-year study on the use of Artesunate for Injection in the U.S.

citations.quote: 3851-5 Conduct a descriptive 5-year study on the use of Artesunate for Injection in the U.S.

requirement.text: 3851-6: Conduct a multiple-dose safety, tolerability, and PK study in pediatric patients with severe malaria from 0 to 12 months of age receiving 2.4 mg/kg Artesunate for Injection.

citations.quote: 3851-6 Conduct a multiple-dose safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK) study in pediatric patients with severe malaria from 0 to 12 months of age receiving 2.4 mg/kg Artesunate for Injection. The majority of pediatric patients in this age group is to be 6 months of age and younger.
